title: Agentic Systems Architect
notes: Design-altitude track for production agentic AI systems. Module spine is the production-hardening 'altitude gap' that intro agent courses skip. Build-altitude fundamentals (agent loops, framework mechanics, RAG implementation) are owned by the lower-level `agentic-ai-engineer` track (level 30) and linked, not duplicated. Languages: examples in both TypeScript/Node.js and Python (agentic dev-tooling is heavily TS/Node). Seeded from role research 2026-06-14; job-market evidence and the verbatim Imagine Learning posting requirements are tracked in JOB_REQUIREMENTS.md / .aicg/job-requirements.json, with a requirement->module traceability map. Refine on first nightly research cycle.

modules.title: Agentic Systems Foundations & When NOT to Use an Agent
objectives: Distinguish workflows from agents and justify the choice per task (predictability vs. model-driven flexibility)
Apply Anthropic's orchestration patterns: prompt chaining, routing, parallelization, orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimizer
Decompose a system into tool vs. sub-agent vs. hardcoded-path boundaries
Frame the 'start simple, add complexity only when it demonstrably improves outcomes' discipline

modules.title: Multi-Agent Orchestration Architecture
objectives: Design orchestrator-worker topologies and reason about their token economics (~15x cost vs. single chat)
Choose between handoffs and manager-as-tools; decide who owns the final user-facing answer
Apply inter-agent protocols (MCP for tools, A2A for delegation) at architecture level
Define escalation and coordination strategies across a multi-agent system

modules.title: Memory & Context Architecture
objectives: Architect context engineering strategies: compaction, structured note-taking, sub-agent isolation, just-in-time retrieval
Diagnose and mitigate context rot in long-horizon agents
Decide where state lives: working/episodic/long-term memory and persistence boundaries
Integrate RAG and vector/knowledge-graph stores as an architectural concern

modules.title: Evaluation Harnesses for Agentic Systems
objectives: Design trajectory evaluation (sequence of messages/tool calls) and final-state evaluation
Build tool-call correctness checks at selection and argument layers (deterministic + LLM-judge)
Author LLM-as-judge rubrics (accuracy, completeness, citation, tool efficiency)
Define an offline/online eval strategy that gates deployment

modules.title: Observability & Tracing for Agents
objectives: Instrument agents with OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions (invoke_agent, execute_tool spans, token attributes)
Distinguish agent observability (output quality, faithfulness, safety, drift) from traditional APM
Architect tracing for non-deterministic, long-running agents across deploys
Evaluate platforms (LangSmith, Langfuse, Arize Phoenix) against requirements

modules.title: Guardrails, Safety & Security
objectives: Design two-sided input/output moderation and per-tool-call guardrails
Mitigate OWASP LLM01:2025 (prompt injection, incl. indirect) and LLM06:2025 (excessive agency)
Apply least-privilege tool access, tool sandboxing, and human approval for high-risk actions
Architect secure authentication and authorization for agent toolchains: OAuth flows, token management, and Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
Design sandboxing and strict permission scopes for local and remote agent/CLI execution to prevent destructive actions or data leakage
Architect segregation of untrusted content and adversarial testing into the system

modules.title: Cost & Latency Architecture
objectives: Model token economics for multi-agent systems and set value thresholds for agentic vs. workflow designs
Apply prompt/prefix caching, model routing, and batch processing as architectural levers
Build cost models and SLAs into a reference architecture
Trade off latency, cost, and quality with explicit budgets

modules.title: Deployment, Durable Execution & Human-in-the-Loop
objectives: Architect durable execution and resumption for long-running, stateful agents (e.g., Temporal)
Design deployment strategies that avoid disrupting in-flight agents (e.g., rainbow deployments)
Integrate human-in-the-loop approval flows (approve/edit/reject/respond) with state persistence
Plan scaling and failure recovery for agent fleets

modules.title: Governance, Compliance & Domain Constraints
objectives: Apply AI governance frameworks (e.g., ISO/IEC 42001) to an agentic architecture
Translate regulated-domain constraints into architecture: data privacy, auditability, accountability
Drive plugin/extension governance for an agentic platform: how plugins are evaluated, versioned, approved, and monitored to prevent unauthorized system changes or quality degradation
Design for sensitive end-users and sectors (e.g., K-12 edtech: FERPA/COPPA, safety for minors, human-in-the-loop on student-facing output, hallucination containment in instructional content)
Produce governance, accountability, and risk-control specifications for agent fleets

modules.title: Agentic Developer Platforms & SDLC Integration
objectives: Design a plugin-based architecture that extends an agentic coding tool (e.g., Claude Code) using its extension standards: Agents, Skills, Hooks, and the Model Context Protocol (MCP)

Architect AI systems for the software development lifecycle: securely interfacing an agent with internal SDLC toolchains and proprietary data to perform requirements analysis, code generation, and debugging autonomously
Build reliable tool-use patterns and context-hydration strategies that give an agent the precise system access and context to execute SDLC tasks
Integrate with core DevOps and project-management toolchains (GitHub, Jira, Confluence, CI/CD pipelines) over REST, GraphQL, and event-driven interfaces
Design developer-focused tooling with a strong emphasis on usability, adoption, onboarding, documentation, and continuous feedback loops

projects.title: Capstone: End-to-End Agentic Reference Architecture
projects.description: Design (and prototype the orchestration of) a production agentic system — e.g., a deep-research or domain agent — that exercises every module: orchestrator-workers topology, memory/context engineering, a trajectory + tool-call eval harness, OTel tracing, two-sided guardrails, a cost/latency model, durable execution, human-in-the-loop, and a governance/compliance spec. Deliverables are an architecture decision record, reference diagram, eval plan, cost model, and threat model.

projects.title: Regulated-Domain Agentic Architecture (e.g., K-12 EdTech)
projects.description: Produce a reference architecture for an agentic system under regulated-domain constraints: FERPA/COPPA data handling, safety guardrails for minors, human-in-the-loop on all end-user-facing output, hallucination containment grounded in vetted content, and toggleable AI features. Frames the governance posture an Agentic Systems Architect must own in a sensitive sector.

projects.title: Agentic AI-for-SDLC Platform (Plugin Architecture)
projects.description: Design a plugin-based platform that extends an agentic coding tool (e.g., Claude Code via Agents/Skills/Hooks/MCP) so the AI can securely interface with internal SDLC toolchains and proprietary data to perform requirements analysis, code generation, and debugging. Deliverables: plugin/extension architecture, secure auth & sandboxing model (OAuth/RBAC/token management, local+remote execution isolation, prompt-injection defenses), a plugin governance lifecycle (evaluate/version/approve/monitor), toolchain integrations (GitHub/Jira/Confluence/CI-CD), and a developer-adoption/DX plan. Mirrors the emerging enterprise 'Agentic Systems Architect' charter.
